title: Manager, AI Risk Management
description:
Location: Towers at SouthPark II, Charlotte North Carolina Position Summary Will support the enterprise AI Risk Management Governance program by executing and enhancing KeyBank's AI risk management framework, risk assessment processes, governance controls, and regulatory oversight activities. This role serves as a central coordinator across business lines, technology, model risk, compliance, legal, information security, third-party risk management, and operational risk functions to ensure AI use cases are identified, assessed, governed, monitored, and deployed in accordance with enterprise standards. Key Responsibilities Based on business needs, this role may be assigned to support any of the strategic initiatives or business-as-usual (BAU) activities outlined below. AI Risk Assessment & Governance (BAU) Lead end-to-end AI risk assessments, including inherent and residual risk evaluation, independent review and challenge, and deployment readiness. Partner across business, technology, risk, compliance, legal, privacy, cybersecurity, and third-party functions to identify and address AI risks. Maintain governance records, reporting, ongoing monitoring, reassessments, remediation actions, and risk decisions. Workflow Adoption Own business requirements and enhancements for the AI risk management workflow within an enterprise GRC platform. Partner with technology teams to design workflows, scoring, reporting, evidence management, and automation capabilities. Lead testing, validation, implementation, and production readiness to maintain a reliable system of record for AI risk decisions. AI Risk Management Framework Implementation Lead implementation of a recognized financial services AI risk management framework and align its requirements to enterprise processes. Coordinate control mapping, gap assessments, ownership, remediation, and evidence standards across business and risk functions. Translate framework requirements into practical policies, procedures, controls, implementation plans, and leadership reporting. Agentic AI & Automation Initiatives Guide the design and implementation of AI-enabled governance, risk assessment, and workflow automation capabilities. Partner with technology teams and external providers to automate evidence collection, control mapping, documentation, and assessment activities. Establish governance requirements, decision gates, human oversight, testing, and monitoring for agentic AI solutions. AI Governance Strategy & Continuous Improvement Advance the AI governance strategy, operating model, policies, standards, and accountability structure. Simplify governance processes and reduce duplication across enterprise risk and control functions. Develop meaningful metrics, risk indicators, dashboards, inventory controls, and management reporting to drive continuous improvement. Stakeholder Management Serve as primary liaison across risk disciplines and first-line business partners. Facilitate working groups, governance forums, and operating committee meetings. Build strong relationships with senior leaders across Risk Management, Technology, Compliance, Legal, and business functions. Drive accountability for risk remediation and control implementation activities. COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS This position is eligible to earn a base salary in the range of $116,000.00 - $216,000.00 annually. Placement within the pay range may differ based upon various factors, including but not limited to skills, experience and geographic location. Compensation for this role also includes eligibility for incentive compensation which may include production, commission, and/or discretionary incentives. Please click here for a list of benefits for which this position is eligible. title: Security Risk & Compliance, Agent Security
description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the team Anthropic's Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) team is the connective tissue that holds the company accountable to its security commitments. We translate regulatory, customer, and voluntary obligations into controls that teams act on, and give leadership a bird's-eye view of how well we're meeting them. We're building toward a fundamentally different kind of GRC: one that directs Claude, with the right humans in the loop, to challenge and evidence the performance of controls continuously rather than through periodic audits. Responsibilities: Serve as the security policy partner for AI agent governance, authoring the policies and standards for how agents are built, deployed, operated Define review and approval criteria when an agent may interact with sensitive or regulated data, and which actions require human approval as it relates to compliance frameworks Serve as the GRC reviewer within existing engineering approval workflows Define data governance requirements for agents, including least-privilege access, access reviews, and handling of regulated and sensitive data Monitor agent behavior over time and adapt governance requirements in partnership with cross-functional security, research and engineering teams Map agent security and data controls to AI governance frameworks (e.g., ISO 27001, ISO 42001, EU AI Act), strengthening Anthropic's certification efforts ensuring agent security is auditable Assess and document agent-related security and compliance risks, driving them to resolution with engineering owners Own the policy for agent-related risk acceptances and exceptions, including approval authority, duration and re-review You may be a good fit if you: Have 8+ years in security governance, risk, and compliance, including ownership of security policies and control standards at a technology company Have owned or meaningfully supported efforts to compartmentalize sensitive data, PII, or intellectual property, and understand how identity and access mechanisms implement or undermine protection boundaries Think about non-human identities as a distinct risk and control category, and can design least-privilege access and accountability controls for systems acting on a person's behalf Can reason from a threat model to a control and explain the tradeoff to both an engineer and an auditor Have defined risk-based review or approval criteria within engineering workflows and kept them effective under high change velocity Deliver clear, precise written work for both technical and non-technical audiences Thrive in ambiguous environments with no settled industry playbook, where you're expected to propose the standard rather than wait for one Are energized by being the security and risk authority who educates and influences outcomes rather than only advises Strong candidates may also: Understand the security properties of LLM agents, whether from an AI, developer-platform, or agent-tooling company, or through comparable experience Bring familiarity with AI governance frameworks alongside traditional security frameworks Have adapted controls from regulated or highly sensitive environments to an open, high-trust engineering culture Possess relevant certifications (CISSP, CISM, CRISC, CISA, CCSP, ISO 27001 or ISO 42001 Lead Implementer/Auditor) Candidates need not have: Done everything on this list before. Very few people have governed AI agents at scale — we care more about how you reason about access, accountability, and blast radius than about a prior title. Deadline to apply: None. Applications will be received on a rolling basis. title: Senior Counsel, Americas Employment
description: Veeam is the Data and AI Trust Company, specializing in helping organizations ensure their data and AI are fully understood, secured, and resilient to enable the acceleration of safe AI at scale. As the market leader in both data resilience and data security posture management, Veeam is built for the convergence of identity, data, security, and AI risk. Headquartered in Seattle with offices in more than 30 countries, Veeam protects over 550,000 customers worldwide, who trust Veeam to keep their businesses running. Join us as we go fearlessly forward together, growing, learning, and making a real impact for some of the world’s biggest brands. #LI-REMOTE #LI-JC2 About the role We’re looking for an experienced, strategic labor and employment attorney to support Veeam’s growing team in the U.S. and throughout the Americas region. This role advises People & Culture and business leaders on the full range of global employment matters, manages employment-related disputes and investigations, and helps build scalable policies and processes to support Veeam’s growth. In partnership with People & Culture, Global Information Security, Finance, and business leaders across multiple jurisdictions, the successful candidate will demonstrate sound judgment, discretion, and the ability to translate complex employment law requirements into practical, business-enabling guidance. What You'll Do Serve as a trusted legal advisor to People & Culture and business leaders on hiring, performance management, leaves of absence, accommodations, terminations, and reductions in force. Advise on compliance with federal, state, and international employment laws, including wage and hour, leave, anti-discrimination, and workplace safety requirements. Provide pragmatic, day-to-day guidance on employee relations issues and sensitive personnel matters, communicating legal risk with a full understanding of business needs. Advise on classification of workers, including exempt/non-exempt status and employee/independent contractor determinations, across multiple jurisdictions. Support expansion into new jurisdictions, including advising on local employment requirements, works councils, and other employee representative bodies, and support immigration-related matters in partnership with outside immigration counsel, including visa sponsorship and cross-border employment issues. Partner with People & Culture on compensation, equity, and benefits programs to ensure legal compliance, including pay equity and pay transparency requirements, while monitoring emerging employment legislation and regulatory developments and translating them into practical readiness plans and policy updates. Manage employment litigation, arbitrations, and administrative charges (e.g., EEOC, state agencies), including strategy, budget, and outside counsel relationships. Advise on separation agreements, severance arrangements, and settlement negotiations, and partner with People & Culture on execution. Provide employment law due diligence and support for M&A transactions, including workforce integration, harmonization of terms, and transition planning. Advise on restrictive covenants, confidentiality agreements, and employee IP assignment provisions in partnership with the IP and Product Legal teams, and manage outside counsel relationships and budgets for employment litigation and specialized advice across jurisdictions. What You'll Bring JD (or equivalent) and active membership in good standing with at least one U.S. state bar. 8+ years of relevant experience, including significant employment law counseling and litigation management experience, ideally within a technology/software company; combination of law firm and in-house experience preferred. Substantive experience advising on U.S. federal and multi-state employment law and experience with international employment matters. Experience managing employment litigation, arbitrations, and agency charges. Experience partnering directly with People & Culture and business leaders in a fast-paced, global environment. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to draft clear policies and present concise, practical guidance to leadership. Experience managing outside counsel relationships and budgets. Bonus Skills Experience supporting global employment law matters across multiple jurisdictions in the Americas. Experience supporting mergers and acquisitions, including employment due diligence and workforce integration. Experience advising on compensation, equity, benefits, pay equity, and pay transparency programs. Experience supporting immigration, visa sponsorship, and cross-border employment matters. Experience partnering with Information Security, Finance, and other cross-functional stakeholders on employment-related initiatives. title: Strategic Project Lead - Healthcare
description: About the Role Appen 's Strategic Project Management team is central to the company's growth strategy, partnering with leading AI companies, frontier model developers, and healthcare technology organizations to deliver the data that makes models work. As Strategic Project Lead, Healthcare, you will lead complex medical AI data programs from solution design through delivery, bridging customer objectives, clinical expertise, and Appen's global delivery capability. This is a hands-on role with visibility across both the customer relationship and the delivery model behind it. Your Impact You'll own the quality and direction of complex healthcare AI programs, translating customer objectives into medical data strategies. Your expertise will establish the standards for how data is designed, evaluated, and delivered. Across Appen's global delivery organization, you'll turn those standards into repeatable approaches, methodologies, and capabilities that support future healthcare AI programs and customer opportunities. Success in this role will create healthcare projects that meet customer and clinical standards, strong customer outcomes, and a growing healthcare data capability that Appen can apply across its portfolio. What You Bring 2+ years in clinical practice, healthcare, medical research, or life sciences, with a track record of leading complex projects or multidisciplinary teams. Strong stakeholder-management skills with the ability to translate ambiguous requirements into clear specifications. Comfortable working in a fast-paced, global environment where priorities and AI capabilities evolve quickly. Nice to Have Experience managing clinicians, researchers, or other specialist professional communities. Familiarity with healthcare data privacy, security, and responsible AI governance. Experience developing or reviewing medical datasets, annotation guidelines, clinical taxonomies, or evaluation criteria. Exposure to AI companies, frontier AI labs, or healthcare technology organizations. Why You'll Love Working Here At Appen, we foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, and excellence. We value curiosity, accountability, and a commitment to delivering the highest quality AI solutions for frontier models. You'll work on complex challenges that shape the future of AI across industries and geographies, alongside talented people in a culture that values humility over ego. You'll have the flexibility to deliver in a way that works for you and your team, supported by tools, resources, and development opportunities to continue to build your capability over time. About Appen Appen has been a leader in AI training data for over 30 years. We specialise in human generated data to train, fine tune, and evaluate models across generative AI, large language models, computer vision, and speech recognition. Our AI assisted data annotation platform and global crowd of more than 1 million contributors in over 200 countries support model pre training, supervised fine tuning, evaluation and benchmarking, safety and red teaming, and multilingual global expansion. title: Senior Consultant Digital- und KI-Strategie & Geschäftsprozesse (m/w/d)
description: Wir sind Liquam – Seit über zehn Jahren optimieren wir Prozesse und digitale Ansätze unserer Kunden oder entwickeln neue Lösungen. Unser kreatives und dynamisches Team besteht aus klugen Köpfen in den Bereichen Beratung, Entwicklung, Marketing und Administration. Was uns vereint, ist die Begeisterung für die digitale Ökonomie und die Chancen, die sie Unternehmen bietet. In einer Welt, die von Technologie bestimmt wird, zeigen wir Unternehmen den Weg zu neuen Erfolgen. Aufgaben Du berätst inhaltlich und technologisch, nicht methodisch. Unsere Kunden bezahlen uns für belastbare Antworten auf die Fragen, was sie konkret tun sollen und ob es funktioniert. Im Mittelpunkt stehen Geschäftsmodelle, Geschäftsprozesse und Technologien im Kerngeschäft unserer Kunden, also die Frage, womit sie Geld verdienen und wie zentrale Unternehmensbereiche wie Vertrieb, Auftragsabwicklung, Einkauf oder Service funktionieren. Digitales Marketing, Social Media und Kampagnen gehören nicht dazu, ebenso wenig reine Projektverwaltung, Moderation oder Change-Begleitung. Du begleitest Unternehmen aller Größen aus unterschiedlichen Branchen, unter anderem Maschinenbau, Industrie und Handel, von der strategischen Ausrichtung bis zur Umsetzung und zum laufenden Betrieb von Lösungen. Du entwickelst gemeinsam mit Geschäftsführung und Führungskreis KI- und Digitalstrategien und prüfst, wie sich Geschäftsmodelle durch Technologie verändern oder neu aufbauen lassen: von Zielbild und Handlungsfeldern über priorisierte Use Cases bis zur Roadmap. Du machst Organisationen fit für KI: mit Grundlagenschulungen für Mitarbeitende, Impulsen und Workshops für Führungskräfte, verbindlichen KI-Richtlinien sowie der Einführung konkreter KI-Lösungen. Du führst Potenzialanalysen durch, einschließlich Interviews, Arbeitsbegleitung vor Ort und Aufnahme der Ist-Prozesse, und bewertest die identifizierten Potenziale nach Nutzen und Aufwand. Du prüfst die Machbarkeit konkreter Anwendungsfälle, einschließlich Tool-Auswahl, Konzeption und Wirtschaftlichkeitsrechnung. Du berätst zu Governance und Compliance beim KI-Einsatz, etwa zum EU AI Act, zur DSGVO und zu Berechtigungskonzepten. Du berätst anbieterneutral bei der Auswahl von Unternehmenssoftware wie ERP-, CRM- oder BI-Systemen, vom Anforderungskatalog bis zur konkreten Empfehlung. Du verantwortest in Umsetzungsprojekten das fachliche Ergebnis: Du klärst Anforderungen, schaffst belastbare Entscheidungsgrundlagen und begleitest die Umsetzung, bis die Lösung beim Kunden tatsächlich funktioniert. Qualifikation Du verfolgst aus eigenem Antrieb, was sich bei KI und Software tut, probierst neue Modelle und Werkzeuge selbst aus und bildest dir ein eigenes Urteil, bevor der Kunde danach fragt. Du berätst aus eigener Erfahrung statt aus Folien. Du stehst hinter dem, was du empfiehlst, und kannst es ohne Fachjargon erklären. Ein Ergebnis ist für dich eine geprüfte Empfehlung, ein funktionierender Prototyp oder ein gelöstes Problem, nicht ein Statusbericht oder ein Workshop-Protokoll. Du hast ein abgeschlossenes Studium oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation und mehrere Jahre Erfahrung in der IT-, Prozess- oder Technologieberatung oder in einer vergleichbaren Rolle in einem Industrie- oder Handelsunternehmen. Du verstehst Geschäftsprozesse in unterschiedlichen Unternehmensbereichen wie Vertrieb, Auftragsabwicklung, Einkauf oder Service und erkennst schnell, wo Automatisierung und KI wirtschaftlich sinnvoll eingesetzt werden können. Du bist mit typischen Systemlandschaften in Unternehmen vertraut und verstehst das Zusammenspiel von ERP, CRM, DMS, BI und weiteren Fachsystemen. Du trittst sicher vor Geschäftsführung und Führungskreis auf und kannst Termine und Workshops eigenständig konzipieren und leiten. Du strukturierst komplexe Sachverhalte sauber und bringst sie in Berichte, Roadmaps und Entscheidungsvorlagen, die auch ohne zusätzliche Erläuterung verständlich sind. Du hast Projekte inhaltlich verantwortet und kannst komplexe Sachverhalte so formulieren, dass unterschiedliche Stakeholder damit arbeiten und Entscheidungen treffen können. Du sprichst verhandlungssicher Deutsch und gutes Englisch und bist bereit, regelmäßig beim Kunden vor Ort zu arbeiten. Benefits Arbeit an aktuellen KI-Themen mit Kunden, die wirklich umsetzen wollen, und Zugang zu neuesten KI-Werkzeugen und Modellen Die ganze Bandbreite von der Strategie bis zur funktionierenden Lösung, mit Ergebnissen, die nicht im Konzept enden, statt jahrelang nur denselben Projektausschnitt zu bearbeiten Projekte direkt mit den Entscheidungsträgern in wechselnden Branchen, Geschäftsmodellen und Systemlandschaften Verantwortung, die mit deiner Leistung wächst, nicht mit deiner Betriebszugehörigkeit Kurze Entscheidungswege und direkter Austausch mit den Geschäftsführern und Gründern von Liquam Flexible Arbeitszeiten, abgestimmt auf deine Kundentermine Strukturiertes Onboarding, exzellentes Arbeitsequipment, moderne Büroräume, regelmäßige Teamevents und Zuschuss zur Altersvorsorge Bitte sende uns Deine Bewerbung über das Bewerbungsformular auf liquam.com oder in Ausnahmefällen per E-Mail an Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Staff AI Data Transformation Architect
description: Our mission at Oura is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles. Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.  At Ōura, we're on a mission to make health a daily practice for everyone. With our award-winning Ōura Ring and app, we've empowered over a million people to improve their sleep, understand their bodies, and transform their health. Now, we're looking for a distinguished AI leader to turn scattered experimentation into safe, scalable, everyday practice across the entire company.We are seeking a Staff AI Data Transformation Architect to lead as the senior-most individual contributor driving Data AI enablement across our Data team at Ōura, reporting to VP, Data Engineering and Analytics. This is a highly visible, org-defining role that combines two things usually split across separate jobs: the strategic work of building a company-wide AI roadmap and operating model, and the hands-on work of running the operational backbone — access, governance, licensing — that makes that practice safe and scalable.There are no direct reports in this role: strategy, influence, credibility, and hands-on execution are your primary tools. This role is distinguished from Senior by its company-wide scope of influence, the level of ambiguity it resolves, and the expectation that you define the problem as much as solve it. What You Will Do: Define and own the Data AI enablement roadmap across data, product, engineering, science and business functions, prioritizing the transformation opportunities with the highest leverage. Build the operating model for repeatable adoption: playbooks, shared tooling, evaluation frameworks, and success metrics that turn isolated pilots into standard practice. Establish a shared language and evaluation framework that leaders across the company use to assess AI opportunities consistently. Drive build-vs-buy decisions for AI tooling, influencing vendor strategy and technology investment at a company-wide level. Own the AI tool estate end-to-end: integration of data and access models within the Databricks platform, multi-agent workflows, token management, and partner with AI Productivity to power the AI ecosystem with a trusted data layer. Hold the governance line: partner with AI Governance, Security, Privacy, and Legal to define guardrails for responsible AI use in a health-sensitive environment, with auditable change management. Keep AI spend efficient: own observability, productivity best practices and reclamation cycles, and the usage insights that inform renewal, expansion, and build/buy decisions. Architect Ōura's Data AI strategy leveraging Databricks and AWS to process terabyte–petabyte scale data with global consistency. Lead the design of machine-readable contracts, vector-based data architectures and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) patterns to enable LLM-powered reporting and Agentic AI at production scale, including an enterprise context plane: ontology, semantic layer, knowledge graph, and context layer. Partner closely with data analysts and engineers to assess, prioritize, and remediate data readiness (quality, structure, access, documentation) against the AI roadmap's use cases. Partner with leadership to drive workflow redesign, working directly with functional leaders to change how their teams operate — not just what tools they have access to. Build internal AI fluency through reusable training, a strong practitioner community, and self-service documentation that let teams and other admins operate independently. Scale a small number of high-value pilots into standard, company-wide practice rather than leaving them as isolated experiments. Act as the primary bridge between executive intent, functional leaders, and enabling functions (Security, Legal, IT, Software). Drive alignment across AI productivity, engineering and business units, establishing trust early and earning a seat at the table through credibility. Set the operating standard that functional AI Champions and any dedicated AI-tool administrators run to, without owning their day-to-day work directly. Represent Data AI enablement in cross-company forums, making adoption and impact metrics visible and discussed at the leadership level. This is a hybrid role out of our San Francisco office.
